headline.conclusion: All 488 rows are external manager entries in the EXTERNAL address space, not real binary functions. Seven imports are directly called by canonical gameplay-category callers, but this proves only an external runtime/support boundary adjacency; it does not make any row gameplay logic or a reconstruction package anchor.

evidence: Every source row has entry=EXTERNAL:######## and va=external:########.
Every source row has is_external=true and canonical=false.
The source reconciliation has containing_block=null, containing_section=null, function_body_size_bytes=null, and no internal function body.
The 488-entry set has zero overlap with the 58,757 canonical function universe and all 58,757 canonical VAs resolve in the live program according to the pinned reconciliation.
No EXTERNAL key appears in the canonical 32-bit SDK function addresses, Track O package anchors, shared-state roots, or vtable slot addresses.
real_function_check.interpretation: External manager entry is an imported symbol/reference entry managed outside the executable's internal function iterator. It is not a binary function body and must not be counted as a function reconstruction target.

identity_reconciliation.resolution: The two xref allowlist entries are outside the requested 488-row scope and are not added to the row index. The 488-row delta remains authoritative for this audit; its 128 null-name rows remain UNKNOWN rather than being matched by inference.

reconstruction_packages.result: No external manager entry is an explicit package function or package root. All listed package anchors/roots are internal 32-bit VAs; external rows therefore are not binary package functions.
reconstruction_packages.compatibility_reason: An imported API can be relevant to a package's host adapter without becoming a reconstructed function or package anchor. The committed artifacts do not establish a per-row package need for these external entries.

shared_state_roots.result: No EXTERNAL entry is a shared-state root. The root contract applies to internal function VAs, not imported symbols.

engine_boundaries.classification_rule: These are OS/runtime/input/timing interface adjacencies named in the engine-boundary evidence; they do not establish gameplay semantics or package ownership.
engine_boundaries.semantic_limit: The boundary match says the external import crosses a documented host/engine seam. It does not say the imported function owns gameplay state, timing values, or event semantics.

triage_categories.result: All 488 entries are outside the canonical triage universe, so their own category is null. Caller categories are reported only for the 7 static gameplay-caller positives below.

sdk_and_vtable.result: SDK functions and vtable candidates are keyed by internal 32-bit addresses. No EXTERNAL entry has an SDK or vtable association.
sdk_and_vtable.caller_context_limit: A gameplay caller may itself be SDK-associated or vtable-associated, but that does not transfer an SDK/vtable identity to the imported EXTERNAL row.

xrefs.result: All 360 named delta entries have static xref evidence. The 128 unknown-identity rows have no joined token and therefore no row-level reachability claim. Xrefs are structural evidence, not runtime reachability.
